Robert Brentano identifies Christopher Brooke at Cambridge as a reviewer of A New World in a Small Place.
Christopher Brooke reviewed Religious and Laity in Western Europe in 2007.

basis: The Malthus article belongs to a Harvard PhD and Cambridge political theorist, whereas the Cambridge medieval historian died in 2015 and had a different career. Key a is mixed: its Rieti review is also attributed to Christopher Brooke at Cambridge, so the medieval review credits should be examined before any merge or split.

evidence.says: Die Wilsnackfahrt (2006) is edited by Felix Escher and Hartmut Kühne; Kühne is a research assistant at Humboldt University of Berlin.
Dr. Hartmut Kühne is affiliated with Humboldt University of Berlin; his contributions include the 15 January 2007 report on Das Zeichen am Hut im Mittelalter.

basis: The publisher places the 2006 book's editor at Humboldt University, and H-Soz-Kult identifies the contributor of the 2007 conference report with the same institution. The matching affiliation and adjacent dates support one career.

evidence.says: Klaus Gietinger wrote the 2014 review of Konrad's Waldemar Pabst 1880–1970 and cites Klaus Gietinger's Der Konterrevolutionär (2009) in a footnote.
Klaus Gietinger's publication list includes Der Konterrevolutionär: Waldemar Pabst – eine deutsche Karriere (2009).

basis: The review cites the book by a namesake, but does not explicitly identify it as the reviewer's own work. The sources found do not independently establish that the two credits belong to one person.

evidence.says: The University of Basel lists Renger’s Narcissus (2002) and Oedipus and the Sphinx (2013).
Freie Universität Berlin lists Renger, Stavru and Stellmacher’s 2015 H-Soz-Kult report on Übungswissen in Religion und Philosophie.

basis: The university bibliography attributes the 2015 conference report on key b to Renger, and the university profile lists books on key a. The report is a conference report, although the graph labels it a review.

evidence.says: Dorit Müller's publications include Gefährliche Fahrten (2004) and her review of Daniela Gretz's Die deutsche Bewegung in H-Soz-u-Kult, 15 October 2007.

basis: The TU Darmstadt publication list attributes both the book on key a and the review on key b to Dorit Müller.

evidence.says: Susan Rimby wrote Mira Lloyd Dock and the Progressive Era Conservation Movement and was dean at Lock Haven University.
In 2013 Susan Rimby was dean of Lock Haven University's College of Liberal Arts and Education.

basis: The book's author held a position at Lock Haven in 2013 and 2016, spanning the 2015 review credited to Susan Rimby of Lock Haven University. The matching institution and years tie the two careers together.

evidence.says: Susan Rimby wrote Mira Lloyd Dock and the Progressive Era Conservation Movement and was dean at Lock Haven University.
The 2025 Seton Hall University review is by Susan Rimby, affiliated with Lock Haven University.

basis: The author of the book and the author of the 2025 review are both identified with Lock Haven University. The historical association's program links the book directly to the dean there; the review metadata supplies the matching affiliation.

evidence.says: Lists Harald Haury as author of Von Riesa nach Schloss Elmau (2005).

basis: The book author is confirmed, but I found no source connecting him to the reviewer of Zwischen Sonne und Halbmond or establishing a shared institutional affiliation in the relevant years. The shared name alone does not establish identity.

evidence.says: Bettina Hinterthür signs the 1999 report on Vertriebene Eliten in Cologne; it identifies Günther Schulz as editor of the conference volume.
Günther Schulz credits Bettina Hinterthür with organizing the 1999 conference and editing its volume.
The 1998/99 Cologne report lists Hinterthür's music-publishing dissertation under Schulz and his Vertriebene Eliten project.
Noten nach Plan by Bettina Hinterthür is identified as her 2004 Bonn dissertation on music publishing in the SBZ/DDR.

basis: The 1999 conference reporter is connected to Schulz's conference as an organizer, while his Cologne research report lists Hinterthür's music-publishing dissertation alongside that same project. The dissertation became Noten nach Plan; the shared supervisor, project and dates make the identification strong but inferred.

evidence.says: Johannes Hund’s publication list includes Das Wort ward Fleisch (2006) and his 17 September 2009 H-Soz-u-Kult review of Neuser’s Johann Calvin.
The 2009 review of Neuser’s Johann Calvin – Leben und Werk in seiner Frühzeit 1509–1541 is credited to Johannes Hund.

basis: The University of Mainz publication list attributes both the book and the specific review to Johannes Hund.

evidence.says: Ross Coen wrote Breaking Ice for Arctic Oil (2012) and worked at the University of Alaska Fairbanks.
The publisher attributes a review of Our Nelson Island Stories in H-Net to Ross Coen.
Ross Coen of the University of Alaska, Fairbanks reviewed White Fox and Icy Seas in Western Historical Quarterly in 2019.

basis: The author of the 2012 book and the reviewer share the University of Alaska Fairbanks affiliation; the 2011 review credit also places the reviewer at that institution alongside the book's publication. The matching name and institutional career support one person, although the sources do not explicitly list the book and reviews together.

evidence.says: Andreas Nierhaus's publications list includes Gottfried Semper und Wien (2007) and his 2012 H-Soz-u-Kult review of Kaiserjubiläum und Kreuzesfrömmigkeit.
The 2012 review of Kaiserjubiläum und Kreuzesfrömmigkeit is by Andreas Nierhaus of the Wien Museum.

basis: The University of Vienna publication list attributes works from both keys to Andreas Nierhaus. The review's own record confirms its authorship.

evidence.says: Felix Wiedemann wrote the conference report published 28 February 2018; his affiliation is the Institut für Altorientalistik, Freie Universität Berlin.
Felix Wiedemann lists Rassenmutter und Rebellin (2007), work at FU Berlin's Institut für Altorientalistik in 2014–2016 and 2019–2022, and a 2018 FU fellowship.

basis: The book's author and the conference report's author are linked by the same FU Berlin institute and overlapping career period. The identification is inferred from the affiliation rather than an explicit listing of both works.

evidence.says: Monika Kubrova, Halle/S., wrote the 2005 report on Arenen der Elitenvergesellschaftung.
Monika Kubrova's Vom guten Leben was published in 2011 and was also a 2009 dissertation at the University of Halle.

basis: The report identifies its author with Halle, and the book originated as a dissertation at the university there. The report does not identify an institutional affiliation, and the sources do not directly connect the two works to one person.

evidence.says: FAU lists Cornelia Scherer's Der Pontifikat Gregors IV. and her 2012–2016 research position on the EPISTOLA project.
The 2013 EPISTOLA conference report is credited to Cornelia Scherer, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg.

basis: The book author's FAU profile places her on the EPISTOLA project in 2012–2016; the 2013 report credits Cornelia Scherer at the same institution and concerns that project. This institutional and dated project match supports one scholar.

evidence.says: Rina C. Faletti co-edited Hydrohumanities, is a UC Merced research affiliate, and teaches art and architecture at California State University, Chico.

basis: The author biography links the Hydrohumanities editor to both UC Merced and California State University, Chico, the institution attached to the review credit. This supports identifying the two keys as the same scholar.

evidence.says: Gregory Brew completed a Georgetown PhD in 2018; his project was Mandarins, Paladins, and Pahlavis.
Gregory Brew received his Georgetown doctorate in 2018 and authored The Struggle for Iran.

basis: SMU identifies the author of The Struggle for Iran with a 2018 Georgetown doctorate, and its fellow profile identifies his project by the title of the dissertation on the other key.
